title: Life from above.
subtitle: New birth, faith in the Son, and the joy of pointing others to Jesus.

quote.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.

composition.text: Often dated AD 85-95 and associated with Ephesus; this dates the Gospel, not the events.
composition.author: Traditionally John the apostle; the author is unnamed.
composition.uncertainty: Dating is uncertain; some Christian scholars argue for before AD 70.

events.text: During Jesus' ministry, after the John 2 Passover scene and before the Baptist's imprisonment (3:24). No exact year is given.

historicalContext.text: Nicodemus is a Pharisee and Jewish leader; purification and baptism matter here. On the later dating, readers lived after Jerusalem's destruction in AD 70.

literaryContext.text: John 2 closes with responses to signs. Nicodemus starts there; Jesus leads him toward new life.

bigIdea.text: God gives new life through the Spirit and eternal life through faith in his Son.

meaning.title: Receive new birth
meaning.text: Knowledge cannot produce new birth. The Spirit gives it; anew can also mean again or from above.

meaning.title: Believe in the Son
meaning.text: The lifted serpent points to the Son. God gives life to believers; light exposes evil and rejection.

meaning.title: Make room for Jesus
meaning.text: John rejoices as people turn to Jesus. The Son speaks God's words; belief brings life, rejection leaves judgment.

interpretiveNote.text: Water and Spirit (3:5): Christians differ between readings including baptism and Ezekiel's promised cleansing.

related.title: Cleansing & a new heart
related.text: God promises cleansing, a new heart, and his Spirit: an Old Testament background for John 3:5-10.

related.title: Look & live
related.text: Those bitten look at the bronze serpent and live. Jesus explicitly draws this connection in John 3:14-15.

related.title: Why John wrote
related.text: John writes to nurture belief in Jesus as Messiah and Son, and life in his name.

questions: Read John 3 aloud. What surprises Nicodemus? What does Jesus say the Spirit does (3:1-13)?
Read Numbers 21:4-9. How does it illuminate John 3:14-18? How do love and judgment fit together?
Compare hiding from light (3:19-21) with John's joy (3:29-30). Where could you practice honesty or humility this week?
application: Choose one response: pray about a hidden struggle, seek a trusted Christian's help, or serve without seeking credit. Revisit it next meeting.
prayer: Father, thank you for your Son. Renew us by your Spirit, help us come into the light, and teach us to rejoice when Jesus is honored. Amen.

sources.title: John 3
sources.identityEvidence: World English Bible chapter text, identified as public-domain Scripture on the page.
sources.supportNotes: Read all 36 verses and notes. Nicodemus visits at night; water/Spirit and anew/from above; lifted serpent; love/light; baptism; Baptist's joy and Son's authority. Does not give an exact event year or say why Nicodemus chose night.

sources.title: John overview
sources.identityEvidence: Page identifies the Bible-teaching ministry of Pastor Chuck Swindoll and his pastoral/seminary role.
sources.supportNotes: Who wrote the book and Where are we sections: Gospel unnamed internally, traditional apostolic authorship, Ephesus and AD 85-95. These are attributed historical judgments, not certain dates stated in John.

sources.title: Guide to John
sources.identityEvidence: Christian Bible education ministry; guide presents Jesus as Messiah and Son of God and reads the Bible as a unified story leading to Jesus.
sources.supportNotes: Overview and John 2-12 section place Nicodemus among signs and encounters; new heart/life, and author's purpose of faith and life. Do not repeat the unsupported all-night embellishment as a textual observation.

sources.title: John 3 commentary
sources.identityEvidence: Pastor David Guzik's Christian commentary; statement of faith affirms Scripture, Jesus Christ and Christian ministry.
sources.supportNotes: Sections A.2-5 and B cover new birth and Nicodemus, competing water readings including baptism and Ezekiel cleansing, serpent analogy, and Baptist witness. Commentary interpretations are kept distinct from Scripture; avoid generalizing its claims about all Jewish expectations.

sources.title: Ezekiel 36:25-27 in context
sources.identityEvidence: World English Bible text and public-domain notice.
sources.supportNotes: Verses 22-28: restoration of Israel, cleansing, new heart and Spirit; connection to John 3 is interpretive and supported by S4.

sources.title: Numbers 21:4-9 in context
sources.identityEvidence: World English Bible Classic Scripture text.
sources.supportNotes: Israel complains, serpents bite, people confess, Moses intercedes and makes the bronze serpent; bitten people looking live. John 3 makes the explicit comparison.

sources.title: John 20:30-31 in context
sources.identityEvidence: World English Bible Classic Scripture text.
sources.supportNotes: Purpose statement follows Thomas and resurrection appearances: selected signs, belief in Messiah/Son and life in his name.

sources.title: John 2
sources.identityEvidence: World English Bible Classic Scripture text.
sources.supportNotes: Cana purification jars; Jerusalem Passover and temple scene; 2:23-25 connects signs and belief to Nicodemus's opening in 3:2.

sources.title: The Gospel of John: Introduction, Argument, Outline
sources.identityEvidence: Christian Bible study ministry publishing Daniel B. Wallace's New Testament teaching.
sources.supportNotes: Date section contrasts 90s and pre-70 dating, mentions Jerusalem's destruction in AD 70, and argues for the earlier view. Late-date context on the handout is explicitly conditional.
